response.sql: WITH line_rates AS (SELECT b.link_to_event AS event_id, CAST(b.spent AS REAL) / b.amount AS rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent <> 0), event_rates AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.type, AVG(lr.rate) AS event_rate FROM event e JOIN line_rates lr ON lr.event_id = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.type), type_rates AS (SELECT type, AVG(event_rate) AS avg_rate FROM event_rates WHERE event_rate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY type) SELECT type, avg_rate AS average_spending_rate, avg_rate / (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) FROM type_rates) AS relative_to_mean_type_rate FROM type_rates;

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines are matched to events with an inner join on budget.link_to_event = event.event_id, so lines with no matching event are dropped.

Lines are excluded when spent = 0; lines with a NULL spent are also excluded because they are missing. Lines with a NULL or zero amount give a NULL rate (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero) and are ignored by AVG.

Each event's rate is the unweighted mean of its line-level spent/amount ratios, and each type's rate is the unweighted mean of its event rates. Events with a NULL type form their own group under GROUP BY.
The divisor is the simple mean of the per-type average rates, computed over types with non-NULL rates. Results are not rounded. The SQL targets SQLite, which the TEXT/REAL schema suggests.
